headline: Norris masters the wet to win in São Paulo
standfirst: Lando Norris won the São Paulo Grand Prix for McLaren, finishing 14.602s ahead of Max Verstappen, with Isack Hadjar completing the podium after 71 laps of Interlagos.

sections.title: The start
sections.body: Lando Norris lined up first on the grid. Antonelli got the better launch and led the field across the line at the end of the opening lap. The biggest winner of the opening lap was Hamilton, up 11 places to 9th.

sections.title: How it unfolded
sections.body: The lead changed hands 3 times. Laps led: Norris (48) and Antonelli (23). Norris took the lead for good on lap 54. The race ran green from start to finish.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body: Norris made 3 stops, running intermediate → soft → intermediate tyres. The field made 58 pit stops in total; the quickest stationary time was 2.1s for Bortoleto on lap 32.

sections.title: Movers
sections.body: Max Verstappen made up the most ground, climbing 19 places from 21st to 2nd. Bearman went the other way, slipping from 6th to 17th. Timing recorded 297 on-track position changes, 27 of them by Hamilton.

sections.title: Retirements
sections.body: Stroll (lap 31) failed to finish. Bottas did not take the start.

sections.title: Conditions and pace
sections.body: A damp track called for wet-weather tyres for part of the distance, although little rain fell during the race itself. Track temperature ranged from 21°C to 30°C, with air at 16–17°C. Kimi Antonelli set the fastest lap, a 1:12.689 on lap 55.
